approach: make copilot-cli a derived-output vendor: plugin build derives com.github.copilot/{agents,commands,rules,hooks/hooks.json,lsp.json} from the canonical manifest and passes an authored extensions/ through; the manifest stays canonical at root plugin.json

scope: the five component kinds the runtime changelog names as moved, plus extensions pass-through. skills/ and mcp.json stay at the plugin root and are out of scope. outputStyles is not a Copilot kind and is out of scope.

knock-on: ADR-0011's 'copilot-cli is warned about, never derived for' rule no longer holds for hooks -- copilot now has a derived hooks file, so an unrepresentable handler is dropped from it rather than reported as ignored at runtime. ADR-0013's dependency rule and the harness-override warning are unaffected: both concern manifest content, and the manifest is still canonical.

freeze handling: two frozen scenarios in plugin/build/build.feature are rewritten (copilot-cli derives nothing; copilot-cli warns an unsupported handler is ignored at runtime). Both assert behavior the runtime has since made wrong. Clearance pre-authorized by the CR, which asks for exactly this reversal.

high blast radius (build engine + doctor + examples + docs + two ADRs' consequences) but a single coherent concern -> auto-all: self-assert both gates within leash after a cold judge passes; Conflict and Compatibility still stop.

why: Copilot CLI becomes a derived-output vendor for its components while its manifest stays canonical (ADR-0015): plugin build derives com.github.copilot/{agents,commands,rules,hooks/hooks.json,lsp.json} from the canonical component paths, renaming agents to the .agent.md the runtime recognizes, and passes an authored extensions/ through. The vendor reports built at the namespace when it derives any of the five kinds and canonical at plugin.json when it derives none; skills/ and mcp.json do not move. ADR-0011 section 3 is wholly superseded (copilot now has a derived hooks file, so an unrunnable handler is dropped from it) and ADR-0004's no-command-surface premise expires. Clearance: two frozen scenarios rewritten rather than extended, both asserting behavior the runtime made false in 1.0.80-0; pre-authorized by the CR, which asks for exactly that reversal. Compatibility: additive on the 0.x line, declared minor in the changeset. Conflict none. Six judge rounds: round 1 blocked at the governance pre-flight (bars loaded, draft re-aligned); rounds 2-5 each failed Builder on one more branch of the same decision stated in prose and unwired from the suite, every one a coverage gap the implementation already satisfied; round 3 also failed Architect on a supersession note that contradicted the paragraph it superseded and a footnote citing the page this ADR calls stale. Round 6 returned ALIGNED true, oracle/builder/architect all passing, and answered the standing question directly: the sweep converged and the missing Control Flow graph is not a precondition.
